totals.rows_scoped: contract.invariants, contract.not_exposed, instructions and best_practices across the 10 cap-layer -implement facets named in the task (cap-mandate-broker-implement, cap-memory-implement, cap-model-access-implement, cap-policy-implement, cap-provenance-implement, cap-scheduling-implement, cap-state-persistence-implement, cap-telemetry-implement, cap-tool-access-implement, cap-work-intake-implement). definition_of_done, adapters and composes_with were off limits per instruction and not touched; open_questions not touched (every row there already carries sources and a quote); the ten cap- ideal facets and every harness/ directory belong to sibling agent 60-cap-sourcing-a and were not read for citation-hunting beyond what the -implement facet's own text already named.

method: For every proposed row in the four scoped sections: ran python3 tools/kb.py show <id> plus grep -i over kb/facts.jsonl (including the F-a* Part A host-fact lens), kb/target-facts.jsonl, kb/reference-facts.jsonl, kb/research.jsonl (each skill's own X-cap-<skill>-* lens) and kb/architecture.jsonl (A-tool-*/A-change-* impact rows, none of which named a row this ceremony touched); kb/decisions.jsonl was read for background only, never cited, since no D- id is a valid citation prefix under schemas/skill.schema.json. Converted to sourced only when a verbatim quote from a cited record supported the row's own specific claim rather than merely sharing vocabulary with it: many rows already carried a background F- or X- citation in their proposed form (a pattern seen throughout this layer, e.g. cap-memory-implement instructions#4's F-a6-01/X-cap-memory-003, cap-policy-implement's per-row F- citations) and most of those stayed proposed because the cited record supports only the row's background, not its specific claim - for example cap-scheduling-implement's F-b3-15 (a bare table row naming RFC 5545) supports the standard but not the four-vector-class or idempotency-key-derivation claims layered on top of it, and cap-work-intake-implement's F-b3-08 supports the canonical-envelope contract but not the specific migration order or field-request discipline built on it. Where a fact did support the specific claim, three kinds of match dominated the conversions: (1) 'today' inventory facts matching a build-order claim directly (F-a6-02's Temporal-orchestrator-server-not-listening finding sourcing cap-scheduling-implement's 'build the standalone evaluator first, not second'; F-a6-03's zero-tools-registered finding sourcing cap-tool-access-implement's 'register the smallest useful tool first'; F-a5-03/F-a5-04's today-state rows sourcing cap-state-persistence-implement's 'two append-only hash-chained stores, neither deleted'); (2) design-rule facts already used elsewhere in this repo for the identical claim shape (F-a7-03 structurally-green and F-a7-04 silently-discarded-configuration sourcing the 'documented conformance subset is honest' and 'verify runtime effect, not the file' rows repeated across cap-policy-implement, cap-provenance-implement, cap-state-persistence-implement, cap-telemetry-implement; F-b1-08 cross-cutting-guarantees-not-optional sourcing wiring rows in cap-provenance-implement, cap-state-persistence-implement, cap-telemetry-implement; F-part-c-08 claimed-versus-measured sourcing the standard end-of-facet evidence rows in cap-scheduling-implement and cap-work-intake-implement; F-part-c-09 products-belong-in-the-adapter-column sourcing not_exposed rows in cap-scheduling-implement and cap-work-intake-implement); and (3) X- research records naming the exact mechanism a row proposed (X-cap-provenance-004's OIDC/Rekor snippet sourcing the keyless-signing adapter; X-entry-composition-050/051's gen_ai.* lifecycle-attribute and Development-stability-badge snippets sourcing cap-telemetry-implement's mapping-adapter design; X-cross-structure-048's optimistic-concurrency snippet sourcing cap-state-persistence-implement's fencing-token invariant; F-a7-02's depth-3-task-tree finding sourcing cap-telemetry-implement's depth-3 fixture practice). Several rows restated their ideal sibling's own not_exposed or invariants row (cap-mandate-broker-implement's two not_exposed rows against cap-mandate-broker's not_exposed#1/#2; cap-memory-implement's scope-predicate invariant against cap-memory's construction-not-filter invariant; the adapter-pair-axis invariant repeated near-verbatim across cap-model-access-implement, cap-policy-implement, cap-provenance-implement, cap-scheduling-implement, cap-state-persistence-implement, cap-tool-access-implement and cap-work-intake-implement) or restated build-adapter-pair's design rule 3 directly without adding a citable extension; each was trimmed to a one-clause proposed pointer naming the sibling or the build-* skill by name, keeping only the row's own implement-specific consequence (a selection criterion, a report-shape requirement) rather than the restated design rule itself - these pointer rows still carry origin=proposed and count toward proposed_after, so they are not counted separately in the totals table, matching how the already-existing 'proposed pointer, see that skill' rows in this same layer (instructions and invariants rows ending 'proposed pointer, see that skill[\'s ...]') were left untouched as already-correct. No row was outright deleted this ceremony: every restatement found had a build-specific residue worth keeping as a trimmed pointer rather than nothing, so deleted=0 across all ten skills, consistent with sourcing-01 and sourcing-02a/2b/2c's own 0-deletion results for this repository's rows. Every row left proposed had a 'Research query:' sentence appended to its action/why or text field naming the specific record or fetched (not search-only) read that would source it - most commonly asking whether the cited background fact, read from its underlying standard rather than the PASS.md table row, would fix a build-level specific this facet currently states as its own design.
quality_note: Every candidate quote was checked as a literal substring of its row's cited kb record (or json.dumps of the record for research.jsonl entries with no text field) before conversion. Cross-skill quote reuse was checked against each edited skill's own composes_with.builds_on chain (build-adapter-pair, build-definition-of-done, build-evidence-record and its own cap- ideal sibling, plus the implicit agentic-stack root) rather than the whole repository: several first-draft conversions collided on (id, quote) with a builds_on sibling already holding that exact quote (F-a7-03 and F-a7-04 against build-definition-of-done in cap-policy-implement and cap-provenance-implement; F-a5-03 and X-cross-structure-048 against cap-state-persistence itself in cap-state-persistence-implement; F-a7-02 against both cap-telemetry and build-evidence-record in cap-telemetry-implement; X-cap-provenance-004 against cap-provenance itself; F-b4-05 and F-a5-03 against build-evidence-record in cap-provenance-implement) and each was fixed either by requoting to a different verbatim substring of the same short record or, where the record was too short to offer a second substring, by naming the colliding sibling explicitly in the row's own prose, then re-running tools/validate_skills.py --only <skill> until the warning cleared. One transcription bug surfaced during this process and was caught and fixed before final validation: three rows in cap-state-persistence-implement, two in cap-scheduling-implement and none elsewhere were briefly written to a stray 'action' key (instructions' field name) on an invariants/not_exposed/best_practices row (which use 'text') by a shared helper script; each was caught by a `if 'action' in row` scan of every edited file and repaired by moving the content to 'text' and deleting the stray key before the final render+validate pass, so no skill.json in this ceremony's scope carries an extra or schema-unrecognised field. tools/render_skill.py and tools/validate_skills.py --only <skill> were run after every edit and again as a final sweep across all ten skills: final result is 0 errors for all ten, and every skill's own warning count and warning text is byte-identical to its pre-ceremony git-HEAD baseline (verified per file with git stash / git stash pop around each validate run) - cap-mandate-broker-implement 4, cap-memory-implement 1, cap-model-access-implement 7, cap-policy-implement 0, cap-provenance-implement 0, cap-scheduling-implement 0, cap-state-persistence-implement 0, cap-telemetry-implement 0, cap-tool-access-implement 8, cap-work-intake-implement 1 - so no new restatement warning was introduced under any of the ten skills' own --only name.
